newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico awards Operadora Biper radioelectric bands.
newsitem.headline: Mexico awards Operadora Biper radioelectric bands.

text.p: Mexico's Communications and Transport Ministry said Wednesday it awarded Operadora Biper a concession to use bands of the government-controlled radioelectric spectrum.

"With the concession, the company assumed the responsibility of offering beeper services with the highest technology to send tone, voice and numerical message to subscribers," the ministry said in a statement.
Operadora Biper is formed of Mexican investors represented by a company called Radiocel, and expected to begin operations in six months through the three-year contract, the ministry said.
The company plans to cover the entire country through bases in 83 cities in Mexico and the use of Mexico's national Solidaridad satellite system.
The ministry's auction of radioelectric spectrum rights is part of a larger privatization scheme of satellites and telephone and transportation networks.
